steps.text: Line a jelly roll pan with waxed paper. Set aside.

Place white confectioners' coating in the top of a double boiler over simmering water. Stir frequently, scraping down the sides with a rubber spatula to avoid scorching, until melted. Transfer to the prepared pan; spread out. Sprinkle jelly beans over top.
Refrigerate until firm, at least 1 hour. Break into pieces to serve.

raw_recipe.headline: Jelly Bean Bark
raw_recipe.description: A delicious jelly bean bark recipe is a simple and delicious spring confection that gets creative with creamy white chocolate and fruity jelly beans.

review.reviewBody: The chocolate referred to in the recipe is the white confectioners' coating. Although they are slightly different, i.e. white chocolate is made with cocoa butter and confectioner's coating is made with vegetable fats. Some people use them interchangeably in certain recipes, especially if it is being used for coating. I think they say the confectioners' coating melts better than the white chocolate itself. Hope this helps! :)

This is outstanding and couldn't be easier! I used Brach's Sour Jelly Bird Eggs (flavors such as watermelon, raspberry, etc). I don't like jelly beans at all, but with the sweet of the chocolate and sour fruity flavor of the jelly beans, I loved it. When I bought my white chocolate melting discs at the candy supply store, they told me they melt their chocolate for dipping and bark by melting it in the oven at 170 degrees! So I put parchment paper on my cookie sheet, put the discs evenly on the sheet and melted the chocolate (170degrees for 15 minutes) took it out, put the jelly beans on top and then used Easter sprinkle that contained the same colors as the jelly beans which helped fill in some of the white areas. I plan to make this every Easter from now on; other adults who don't like jelly beans also loved it! Thanks for sharing such a fun recipe!

I did this a bit differently. I put liners in a minicupcake pan (got this idea from the pictures) then I dropped a small mini twist pretzel in the bottom. I melted the white chocolate, poured it on top, and then put jelly beans on top. The salty sweet is delish!

I made this as the Recipe Group recipe for the week of March 22nd. EDIT: I made this again this year, only this time I used Ghirardelli white chocolate bars, which I melted in a nonstick pot on the lowest heat setting on my stove top, stirring constantly. Still used Starburst jelly beans -- they still look to be the best option out of a bad lot at the grocery store, but I digress. I still find that 1 pound of chocolate didn't stretch all the way across the pan and would double or triple it next time if using a jellyroll pan. This year I scored lines into the candy where I want it to break instead of just leaving that up to fate, because didn't do me any favors with the shapes last year. This is a SUPER cute idea & I wish I'd thought to buy candy molds this year! Thanks again, Christina!

Well this is VERY sweet! I used a bag of white chocolate chips, melted it in the microwave, and then added whole almonds to my chocolate before I poured it out on a wax paper lined cookie sheet. Worked just great! I added about 1/2 a bag of jelly beans and stuck it in the freezer for maybe 10 minutes. Doesn't get more simple than that, but I next time I might add some pretzel pieces too.

Surprisingly good. All the kids loved this! So easy too. I tried some with choc bark- not so great. Def stick with the white choc. I alos did some with PB MnMs and the jellybean ones (starburst) were the best. I even made a few in some egg molds- really cute for Easter and some others in a lined mini muffin pan. Very sweet though so a little goes a long way.
Excellent and so easy! I used white chocolate chips I melted in the microwave which made prep easier. This will be a standby for Easter going forward!

I made this with my DS. I gave him the kitchen scale so he could measure out the ingredients. We mixed 2 kinds if starburst jellybeans and used exactly a pound. We also used 1 lb of Wilton Cabdy melts which is just shy of 1 1/2 bags. I melted the candy in a double boiler since I prefer that method to the microwave. DS spread a thin layer of candy melts onto a foil lined jellyroll pan. The candy melt layer was 1/8 inch or less. The jellybeans were the smaller size which I think works best since the candy melt layer is thin and probably wouldn't hold large jellybeans well. The refrigeration time was much less than an hour. We had no trouble breaking the bark into pieces. It turned out quite cute. Cuter than I expected. DS loved it and so did DH. so family gave it an A+. Will make it part of our Easter traditions. Thanks Christina for the fun recipe. :-)

Oh this was soo much fun!!! I used my Perfect Brownie Pan, line the pan with foil, then pour in the melted almond bark, then put in the divider and added my jelly beans. Put in the refrigerator and I popped them out when then they were cool, I will so do this again like this, because they were just perfectly uniform and soo pretty.

I have to admit - I'm not a fan of white chocolate, but this is just a brilliant idea. I did 2 batches - one w/ white chips and jelly beans, and 1 w/ "Special dark" chips and Easter M&Ms. They were both gorgeous and so yummy!!! It was funny watching the big burly men chowing down on such a dainty treat. A tip - if you want to use real white chocolate chips, put all the chips minus 1/4 cup in a bowl, nuke at 50% power in 30 second bursts...stirring in between. When it's smooth and creamy, add the last 1/4 cup chips and stir like mad!! This will keep it from melting from the heat of your hand after it's cooled. I can't wait to do this for halloween with orange and black beans!!

Jellybeans are one of my favorite candies. I love Easter time when all of the different varieties are in the stores. So when came across this recipe, I couldn't wait to try it. I decided to go with jellybeans that would have a litte more tartness than the really sweet ones to add some contrast with the white chocolate. I made these in a paper lined mini muffin tin to make them already individual size. The kids and I loved these and you can really play around with the flavors with all of the different jellybeans out now.
I loved it and so did my school 67
YUMMY! I thought the textures mixed together would be weird. It’s not. I microwaved Ghirardelli white wafers and topped them with starburst THE REDS. O EM GEE.
Just added sprinkles because, why not!?!!
This was sooo easy to make! I just finished these for a bake sale at our elementary school. Absolutely adorable! I doubled the recipe & spread it all out on a half sheet pan(approx. 17x13). Perfect!
So cute, easy & fun to make with the kids. Thank you Christina!
So super to make and kids love them.
Made this with my 2 year old son for a family gathering. Not only did my son LOVE sprinkling the jellybeans but all the kids loved eating it. Will make again.
Way too sweet, disappointing. For photography, this recipe is great. Way overdone.
This does turn out pretty, but waaay to sweet. I'll stick to making white chocolate and/or candy melts with something salty like pretzels.
